source.database: Soft Robotics Materials Database (Marechal et al.)
source.paper: Towards a Common Framework and Database of Materials for Soft Robotics (UCL Discovery id 10112846)
source.test_standard: ASTM D412 (Die C dumbbell), uniaxial tensile pull-to-failure, 450 mm/min, room-temperature cure, nominal mix ratio
source.lab: Univ. Savoie Mont Blanc - SYMME Lab, Annecy, FR
source.data_license: ODC Open Database License (ODbL) — vendored raw data retains ODbL, see raw-tensile/README.md

method.model: Ogden 3-term, incompressible, TRUE (Cauchy) stress, uniaxial tension
method.true_stress_formula: sigma_true = sum_i mu_i * (lambda^alpha_i - lambda^(-alpha_i/2)),  lambda = exp(true_strain)
method.fit: scipy minimize(trust-constr), SSE objective, constraint mu_i*alpha_i > 0 (stability), tol 1e-12, init mu=alpha=1. Re-run locally from the vendored raw CSV via scripts/fit_ogden.py (reproducible).
method.warning: Coefficients are for TRUE stress-strain (per source). FEA solvers expect true data. Do NOT plug into engineering-data pipelines without converting.

crosscheck.verdict: MATCH — Ogden eng-stress at break reproduces both the measured curve and the Smooth-On datasheet tensile (200 psi).

soft-clay-10a.model: Ogden N=3 (degenerate: all three alpha collapsed to 2.2704 — terms effectively summed; fit still R2=0.99957). Consider 2-term refit if numerics matter downstream.

crosscheck.verdict: MIXED — Ogden faithfully reproduces the MEASURED curve (1.844 MPa, R2=0.99957), but the measured specimen broke ~43% below the Smooth-On datasheet tensile (475 psi). Not a fit failure: real specimen/batch behavior, consistent with the source paper's thesis that manufacturer datasheets are unreliable for soft elastomers.
